claim: Authors report >95% of their teacher retrieval-heavy performance after preserving ~2% of attention heads in a selected hybrid.
caveat: Retrieval-heavy evaluation, distillation/model selection may not transfer to other tasks.

claim: Olmo 3 published a 7B staged training flow with broad pretraining, targeted midtraining and long-context stage.
caveat: Results are from a full-scale published training recipe, not a small-model replication.

claim: Ai2 reports roughly 2.7× higher training throughput than its earlier MoE stack in a particular eight-B300 comparison.
caveat: Specific hardware, workload and implementation; not a universal MoE multiplier.

claim: DeepSeek-V3 reports approximately 671B total/37B active parameters and 14.8T pretraining tokens.
caveat: Author technical report, not independently reproduced here.

claim: Qwen3 describes switchable think/non-think modes and an inference thinking budget.
caveat: Behavior and token budgets depend on checkpoint/harness; no advantage for our controller proven.

claim: Kimi K2 describes MuonClip stability changes and environment-based posttraining.
caveat: Reported gains cannot be isolated to optimizer without ablations.

claim: Peer-reviewed byteification uses a two-stage retrofit of an existing global subword model into byte-local components.
caveat: Character gains and speed tradeoffs depend on model and evaluation.

claim: Memora's authors report that persistent agent memories often reuse outdated facts during evolving interactions.
caveat: Benchmark covers selected user-like tasks and model samples.

claim: AMA-Bench extends memory evaluation to long-horizon environment/tool trajectories with causal context.
caveat: Study reports specific performance metrics; generalization not established.

claim: Mem2ActBench shows memory-aware agents still struggle to use remembered context to ground tool actions.
caveat: Tasks may reflect synthetic tool and interaction schemes.

claim: Sigma's authors describe a continuous latent diffusion LM warm-started from autoregressive weights.
caveat: Competitive benchmark scores may demand many denoising steps; no speed superiority assumed.

claim: Clock Diffusion proposes block/sliding-window continuous diffusion and caching strategies for language.
caveat: Unclear whether efficient across practical context and batch regimes.

claim: Large empirical study reports that moderate mixes of rephrased synthetic and natural data can help in particular training regimes.
caveat: Optimal ratio depends on budget, model and generator; avoid universal 30% prescription.

claim: Authors describe repetition-aware optimal mixing of limited target-domain data with generic data.
caveat: Tolerance to repetition is source and compute dependent.

claim: A 2026 position paper challenges common broad claims that recursively synthetic training inevitably collapses.
caveat: Position paper reflects one interpretation and does not invalidate other failure conditions.

claim: A 2026 study finds that biased selection/verifier data can suppress rare distribution modes during synthetic data training.
caveat: Depends on assumed data-silo and selection regime.

claim: Ai2 describes auditing approximately 100 models and 34K+ questions to separate benchmark skill dimensions.
caveat: Lab analysis of selected benchmark suite, not proof every capability is measured.

claim: Agent World Model authors describe ~1,000 code/database-backed simulated task environments.
caveat: The number of simulated worlds does not establish cross-domain transfer.

claim: ICLR 2026 RLP explores information-gain-based exploration objectives late in pretraining.
caveat: Improvement may depend on task/data and training compute.

claim: BRIDGE authors report improved mathematical reasoning scores from cooperative SFT/RL optimization.
caveat: Author-reported gains on selected benchmarks, with model and compute confounds to check.

claim: DAPO proposes clipped-policy and sampling modifications for RL on objective reasoning tasks.
caveat: Reported scores are author findings and task/verifier-specific.

claim: Systematic diffusion-LM analysis reports performance changes with denoising steps, blocks and sampling choices.
caveat: Differences need matched end-to-end latency and model weights to attribute to architecture.

claim: Task-sufficient world model study links active probing with structured state discovery.
caveat: Still requires tests on held-out rule and dynamic combinations.

claim: Authors report some reasoning posttraining procedures can reduce the exploration achieved via higher temperature.
caveat: Model and benchmark specific; intermediate-layer decoding may add cost.

claim: v2 full text reports 47/658 PutnamBench problems solved for the 671B model at Pass@1024, whereas the arXiv landing abstract displayed 49/658 at inspection.
caveat: Version and representation mismatch; result remains author-reported and sample-intensive.

claim: Paper v2 documents a Lean 4.9.0 apply? interface bug accepted some invalid 7B apparent proofs; the authors revised earlier success claims.
caveat: Not evidence every remaining result is invalid; demonstrates a checker vulnerability in that setting.

claim: Paper reports 82.4% miniF2F-test Pass@32 and 88.9% Pass@8192 for 671B CoT; these are different sampling budgets.
caveat: Neither number is one-shot accuracy, actual compute cost is not controlled across compared papers.

claim: Free-MAD authors report conformity and majority-vote failure modes and propose scoring full debate trajectories without forced consensus.
caveat: Performance improvements depend on selected models, tasks and cost budgets.

claim: A 2026 multi-agent debate study reports that persuasive incorrect agents degrade aggregate accuracy in its tested setups.
caveat: Adversarial setup is not a universal estimate of failure across all agents.

claim: Neural classifier paper reports miscalibration and benefits of validation-fit temperature scaling in its experimental settings.
caveat: Classification score calibration may fail under domain shifts and does not imply generative answer calibration.

claim: Graph-learning study characterizes graph distinctions that some message-passing GNNs cannot represent.
caveat: Theoretical expressivity bound concerns chosen model classes and is not a global limitation on all AI.

claim: ICLR 2026 speech-language study reports controlled gains from data preprocessing, synthetic data and audio/text sequence composition.
caveat: Study-specific training corpora and models; no reproduction in this repo.

claim: 2026 IJCAI paper proposes separate calibration of retrieved knowledge evidence and downstream reasoning confidence.
caveat: Reported improvements are author-measured on selected knowledge tasks; transfer unproven.

claim: 2026 formal problem-solving paper distinguishes proving a supplied statement from deriving a witness and its proof.
caveat: Automatic evaluation may still depend on formal problem fidelity and tool correctness.

claim: Flow-Lenia authors report raw count and non-neutral evolutionary activity greater in food/dissipative than vanilla, but mass-normalized ranking reverses.
caveat: Raw activity is confounded by differing total matter; these are simulations and neither metric verifies functional heredity.

claim: Flow-Lenia evolutionary experiment uses 500,000 steps, five random seeds, spatial mutation beams and exact parameter vectors as component/species identities.
caveat: Near-identical vectors count as distinct species; phenotype and genealogy are not independently established.

claim: Flow-Lenia OpenES optimization for motion, obstacles and chemotaxis uses externally predefined fitness functions.
caveat: Externally optimized behaviors cannot be credited to an intrinsic no-task evolutionary process.

claim: PBT-NCA v2 explicitly selects worlds under archive descriptor novelty plus DINOv2 visual diversity, with inner gradient objective for territorial aliveness.
caveat: Designer-provided selection signal and visual embedding bias prevent treating chosen morphology as unscripted intrinsic life.

claim: PBT-NCA reports population 30, 500 meta-iterations, 12 inner updates, replacement fraction .25 every five iterations, with three seed runs for reported curves.
caveat: Finite meta-optimization budget and learned world copying are not evidence of independent organism reproduction or indefinite innovation.

claim: PBT-NCA seven-agent condition reports EP near 1 and effective complexity around 0.21±0.05 on its chosen entropy/compressibility metrics.
caveat: Coexistence and spatial pattern scores are metric-dependent and do not demonstrate inherited new ecological functions.

claim: ToLSim evaluates 20 runs of 2 million steps; raw cumulative activity appears unbounded in 8, bounded in 4 and unclear in 8.
caveat: Finite trajectories were classified by sight, so no mathematical claim of infinity or universal system inability follows.

claim: ToLSim gene-component shadow-normalized total and median activity are bounded in all 20 runs and new evolutionary activity is never persistently positive.
caveat: Conclusion depends on gene-valued components, neutral shadow design and selected environment regime; agents/species were not tested as components.

claim: ToLSim neutral shadow model mirrors birth and death counts but chooses random components and periodically resets its state to real population.
caveat: Normalization tests adaptive persistence versus one synthetic neutral process and cannot alone verify ecological new function.

claim: Outlier rule emerged from a genetic-programming search in a 2^140 rotationally symmetric binary CA rule space, using an externally designed novelty score.
caveat: The initial transition physics was externally discovered, even though recurring patterns arise without placing a finished organism.

claim: Original Outlier article reports replications on large sparse grids and a regime change across initial live-cell density thresholds around 0.02 and 0.15 for a 1024x1024 grid.
caveat: Thresholds depend on grid size, environment and finite test configuration; they do not establish robust open-ended heredity.

claim: Outlier clusters repeat around 143 steps and higher-level formations around 1556 steps; the expanding complex ultimately collides or saturates the grid.
caveat: Periodic appearance alone can be an attractor and is not an independently branching offspring lineage under stronger later criteria.

claim: Of 140 rotationally distinct isolated 3x3 Outlier seeds, two join its dominant recurrence trajectory; examined one-bit rule flips did not yield the replication property.
caveat: These are source-reported observations on a selected rule and do not quantify general probability of life-like evolution.

claim: Hintze and Bohm report 15 generations of exact-pattern c2 self-replication in Outlier, using a necessary-cause lineage graph rather than shape resemblance.
caveat: Authors traced a selected deterministic seed, not all rules, and measured exact-copy replication rather than heritable adaptive novelty.

claim: The 2026 follow-up reports a 20,000-tick 1024-square Outlier run producing 31,959,320 cluster instance nodes and 65,552,995 causal edges.
caveat: Large ancestry graph and 966,208 distinct cluster patterns do not alone demonstrate new evolved ecological functions.

claim: Hintze and Bohm report 433 c0 first-generation copies without c0 grandchildren, while c2 exhibits multi-generation branching and distinct temporal pathways.
caveat: Replicator classification is sensitive to specific cluster identity, selected seed, and exact-copy versus functional heredity semantics.

claim: The follow-up identifies c2-like replicators derived from collision debris not on the original c2 lineage, showing recombination of developmental causal routes.
caveat: Authors' new trajectories are not a demonstrated evolving instruction set or adaptation to previously unavailable functions.

claim: The causal lineage tracing includes minimal necessary predecessors for live-cell activations while excluding histories of dead cells.
caveat: Unmodeled negative constraints could alter causal identity in other CA physics; study is not a universal origin-of-life proof.

claim: Stepney's engineering overview proposes autopoiesis, agency and open-ended adaptation as candidate top-level requirements.
caveat: Conceptual framework/requirements, not empirical evidence that a known virtual ALife system satisfies all three or universal agreement.

claim: An ALIFE 2026 late-breaking abstract reports initial Physis automata-chemistry studies where code and language may change, after CPU-to-GPU port.
caveat: The three-page abstract does not establish long-horizon, inherited new operator functions, and no implementation was reproduced here.

claim: Stepney's 2025 complete overview proposes autopoiesis, agency and open-ended adaptation as three high-level engineering requirements, separated from system design and implementation.
caveat: These are author-proposed requirements, not a consensus theorem or empirical demonstration of life.

claim: The 2025 engineering review states that virtual artificial-life systems meeting all proposed full-life requirements have yet to be shown.
caveat: A review's assessment depends on definitional premises, literature coverage and the possibility of partial rather than full life.

claim: Stepney distinguishes variation within a model, innovation changing the model, and transformation changing the meta-model when discussing open-ended novelty.
caveat: The model/meta-model distinction is observer- and representation-relative; it is not a direct measurement of new ecological function.

claim: In a 100-trial parasite-evasion comparison, stochastic-binding Stringmol evaded parasites 32 times, versus zero trials for sticky deterministic-binding Stringmol.
caveat: Study-specific parasite and binding designs; the reported Mann–Whitney QNN p-value evaluates a different outcome statistic.

claim: Stringmol 2016 finds unbound-only decay can select infinite-loop bound molecule complexes that survive without useful ongoing reproduction.
caveat: A modeled decay-regime loophole, not a claim that bound complexes universally dominate chemistry or natural biology.

claim: Length-dependent Stringmol decay can select longer programs and populations whose compute costs become prohibitive for study.
caveat: Author's outcome depends on selected decay rates, sequence representation and simulated population dynamics.

claim: Stringmol UCA authors report 39 viable molecular population takeovers from 500 containers, with 32 involving changes to copier or expressor.
caveat: These are manually identified author experimental events in a hand-seeded artificial chemistry, not replication by AI-Research.

claim: Authors show that changing an expressor can change the meaning of the same genome and yield a viable changed copier, expressor or payload set.
caveat: Changing genomic interpretation demonstrates bounded semantic closure, not independent organismal ecological adaptation.

claim: The 2017 UCA study reports bureaucratic death: proliferation of mutually incompatible expression molecules can collapse otherwise viable replication networks.
caveat: A source-specific system-level failure; the paper does not establish every mutable interpreter is unstable.

claim: The initial 2017 Stringmol UCA requires hand-designed genome, copier and expressor molecules (50 each initially) and an inert HELLOWORLD payload.
caveat: This system is not a de novo artificial protocell; external simulation physics and input state remain crucial.

claim: Physis 2003 evolves interpreter instruction definitions in some offspring, but the original processor structure remains above ninety percent of studied populations.
caveat: Five experiment repetitions and the specified 200k-update horizon cannot prove that structural evolution is impossible.

claim: Physis compares no-external-task reward with an arithmetic-task-reward regime and reports no observed superiority of evolutionary potential versus fixed processors.
caveat: Extra CPU task bonuses are designer-assigned; no observed advantage on these tasks does not settle all potential new environments.

claim: The 2020 Stringmol paper distinguishes type-0 variation within a model, type-1 innovation requiring a revised model, and type-2 emergence requiring a revised meta-model.
caveat: Novelty classification depends on the scientist's chosen starting model and meta-model; this study reconstructs prior observations rather than generating new experimental runs.

claim: Stringmol 2020 calls its reaction-network/hypercycle type-2 novelty EXTRINSIC because the network is added to the observer's scientific meta-model rather than implemented as a new engineering construct.
caveat: An observer's new category is not evidence that a program has internally evolved a new virtual-machine instruction or distinct physical law.

claim: Stringmol 2020 calls several mutation-derived no-product, overwritten-product and multiple-product reaction modes intrinsic model-level innovation.
caveat: Different product outcomes can be a consequence of mutated molecular programs under fixed substrate semantics, not guaranteed adaptive new ecological capabilities.

claim: In the 2020 analysis, reciprocal Stringmol hypercycles require a relation/network-level description: A copies B and B copies A while neither individually copies itself.
caveat: Hypercycle example draws on prior Stringmol studies; the 2020 paper does not report a newly measured rate of network formation or sustained organismal life.

claim: The 2020 Stringmol paper notes that starting with a richer model already containing network interactions changes whether the same observed behaviors qualify as higher-type novelty.
caveat: A model-relative classification must not be treated as an observer-independent measurement of unbounded creative potential.

claim: The authors' ALIFE 2026 abstract reports a Physis CPU-to-GPU port and initial studies of systems whose code and computational language can change.
caveat: Complete three-page conference text and experiment parameters were not reliably inspected here; abstract contains no quantitative results or proof of evolved new ecological functions.

claim: The 2021 spatial Stringmol paper reports 20 runs of which 12 populations had become extinct and eight were still executing at two million timesteps.
caveat: The finite-time survival comparison is author-reported in accessible published summary; no full E2 statistical or code audit in this pass.

claim: Banzhaf and colleagues define open-ended novelty using variation, innovation and emergence levels relative to model and meta-model structures.
caveat: This 2016 paper has only primary abstract and bibliographic verification in this pass; model taxonomy is a conceptual framework, not proof of limitless innovation.

claim: Spatial Stringmol researchers ran 20 independently seeded worlds to 2 million steps; 12 populations died out while eight were still active.
caveat: Survivors were a selected subset and the study had a finite horizon; this is an author-reported experiment, not evidence of indefinite evolution.

claim: The 2021 experiment crossed 100x125 versus 250x50 toroidal grids with block versus dispersed-pair seed placements, using five replicates per cell.
caveat: The 2x2 factorial uses only twenty worlds and a hand-coded 100-replicator ancestor; generalization to other geometries or unseeded origin is unjustified.

claim: Evolved Stringmol parasites induced replicator non-complementary binding, self-scanning and partner-directed copying defenses that can slow replication.
caveat: Adaptive mechanism is reported by authors under designed Stringmol opcodes, spatial physics and decay; it does not create new interpreter primitives or prove self-maintenance.

claim: An evolved self-scanning Stringmol program may effectively increase mutation opportunities by executing a copy operator over its own code before partner copying.
caveat: This changes mutation exposure through evolved code behavior, rather than changing the simulator's primitive point-mutation probability or demonstrating continuous useful innovation.

claim: The 2021 Stringmol study traces macro-scale sequence rearrangements to shifted binding, copying and cleavage behavior despite the engine supplying only basic mutation operations.
caveat: These are limited mechanistic examples from selected lineages and are not demonstrated novel fundamental physics or independently reproduced experimental results.

claim: The authors classify replicator and parasite reaction types by replaying pairs with mutation disabled and report Stringmol 0.2.3.4 with Rstringmol 0.3.1 analysis.
caveat: Exact analysis release version 0.3.1 was not retrieved; inspected current package manifest says 0.1.0 and historical simulator README describes older 0.2.2 despite tag 0.2.3.4.

claim: Banzhaf and coauthors define Type-0 variation as within-model, Type-1 innovation as changing a model, and Type-2 emergence as changing a meta-model.
caveat: The levels depend on the scientist's definitions and initial taxonomy; this conceptual work does not report independent newly evolved organism functions.

claim: Banzhaf and colleagues call explicit simulator individuality a major shortcut that prevents demonstrating the emergent origin of the identity supplied by that shortcut.
caveat: This is a modeling and causal attribution argument, not evidence that such simulations are scientifically invalid for all other properties.

claim: The 2016 framework describes external copy and explicit fitness as shortcuts that pre-install reproduction or a selection objective in the simulated world.
caveat: Models with such operations may still reveal other mechanisms, but cannot credit those preinstalled properties to autonomous lower-level emergence.

claim: The 2016 full article distinguishes externally observed novelty, pre-coded recognizers, pre-coded structural shortcuts, emergently generated recognition code and new executable shortcuts.
caveat: These five options are proposed theoretical architectures, not five demonstrated implementation successes or verified living-system transitions.

claim: Banzhaf and coauthors emphasize that finite base resources constrain hierarchical novelty and distinguish theoretical from effectively open-ended finite-horizon behavior.
caveat: Neither endless running nor a long period of innovation proves open-endedness to infinity; the proposed hierarchical model is not shown universal across domains.

claim: Stepney and Hickinbotham report retrospectively applying several novelty metrics to eight surviving long-running spatial Stringmol worlds to illustrate limits of fixed measures.
caveat: Only the primary abstract and metadata have been reviewed here; no complete method or new analysis recalculation, so evidence remains E1.

claim: Furubayashi and coauthors report 120 rounds of wet-lab host–parasite RNA replication with diverging host and parasite lineages and antagonistic adaptation.
caveat: Physical RNA/protein replication differs fundamentally from digital Stringmol; original quantitative wet-lab protocols were not independently audited or reproduced here.

claim: Full 2020 bacterial paper reports separated propagules increasing group offspring fitness (χ²=32.660, p<0.0001) while cell-density fitness decreased (F=10.612, p=0.002).
caveat: Original separated arm was included in 2014 paper; do not count as independent validation; engineered life-cycle structure.

claim: Full 2020 bacterial paper reports mixed propagules increasing constituent-cell fitness (F=56.214, p<0.0001) but no significant group offspring improvement (p=0.077).
caveat: Group fitness is relative offspring output proxy; environmental mixing changes selection and can reduce between-group diversity.

claim: Authors report stable multicellularity in 4 of 12 algae populations under predation and 0 of 12 under settling after about 600 generations; earlier transient clusters failed persistence tests.
caveat: Two selection arms not a general proof settling cannot evolve multicellularity; 6 isolates are not 6 independent evolutions.

claim: Sequenced representative multicellular algae isolates traced to two of ten mixed founding strains; authors did not reconstruct causative mutations or measure founder competitive sorting over time.
caveat: Only 4 isolates sequenced from 6 stable isolates; initial-genotype competitive selection remains alternative explanation.

claim: Authors report that the initial lambda-expression generator profoundly changes AlChemy self-organization outcomes, sometimes favoring inert identity-function populations.
caveat: Designed reductive rules, generator and total-population replacement still act as external simulator substrate.

claim: Authors study 455 pairwise combinations of evolved L1 AlChemy organizations and report higher coexistence uncommon relative to domination or mutual destruction.
caveat: Set-overlap coexistence not group reproduction, and single-world spontaneous L2 origin not comprehensively tested.

claim: 2019 algae study authors report multicellularity in 2/5 predator-exposed evolution populations after ~750 generations, absent in predator-free controls.
caveat: Different evolution population/history from 2025, though organisms and some investigators overlap; full main methods not reviewed to E2.

claim: 2024 theoretical metapopulation model reports evolutionary hysteresis stabilizing selected collective traits after changing scaffolding parameters.
caveat: Model patch structure and reproduction still externally imposed; parameter reset does not establish autonomous scaffold-free life.

claim: 2025 review argues artificial community selection often fails because collective traits are not reliably inherited; proposes positive interactions, functional integration and entrenchment.
caveat: A review and proposed framework, not a new microbial selection experiment or validated universal metric.

claim: 2012 yeast experimental evolution paper reports all ten selected populations developed snowflake clusters after 60 rounds of settling selection.
caveat: External settling selection and yeast cellular physiology already provided; full paper not reviewed to E2 in this pass.

claim: Giger 2024 induced Mycetohabitans transmission to nonhost fungal spores; initially ≤4% positive spores after implantation.
caveat: Human-injected bacteria and existing host spores are externally provided reproductive machinery; one founder yielded ten derived lines.

claim: Following ten directed selection rounds, fungal positive-spore germination improved from ~6.3% to ~75%, with metabolic rhizoxin products detected.
caveat: Selection explicitly enriched bacteria-bearing spores; index/chemical transfer does not demonstrate endogenous group reproduction or net ecological benefits.

claim: Without FACS positive selection, even evolved fungal-bacterial associations dropped below propagation threshold after four to five rounds; ancestral pair within one.
caveat: A finite short washout period; different resource/ecological selective environments not assayed; does establish negative under tested conditions.

claim: Reinjecting ancestral bacteria into an evolved fungal host retained improved germination, while sequencing found enriched host genetic changes.
caveat: Crossover and gene-frequency correlations support host adaptation but no causative allele-specific reconstruction; fungal epigenetic factors unexcluded.

claim: Krishnan 2026 formal model reports stable ectosymbiotic mutant invasion when attached partner reduces host inhibition from self-produced toxic byproducts.
caveat: Model assumes fixed U and Y waste metabolism and a preexisting attachment mutant Z; no independently reproducing ecological unit demonstrated.

claim: Authors preinstall consortial reproduction and random symbiont assortment and do not model interspecific attachment/dissociation dynamics explicitly.
caveat: Theory does not establish evolving reproductive interface, vertical co-inheritance or a new physical/digital autonomous organism.

claim: Fisher 2017 comparative study includes 106 host bacterial pairings from 89 host and 58 bacterial-symbiont taxa with phylogenetic controls.
caveat: These are overlapping literature pairings and host experiments, NOT 106 independent laboratory origins of endosymbiosis.

claim: Mean host fitness cost of symbiont removal correlates with vertical vs horizontal transmission (~52% vs ~21%) in source comparison.
caveat: Only plotted subset N=38, heterogeneous fitness measures and taxonomic/sampling bias; association not transmission causation.

claim: Inside-cell symbiont location did not independently predict statistically greater host dependence in tested comparative models.
caveat: Phylogenetic and sampling limitations; physical enclosure cannot be equated with reproductive cohesion or organismhood.

claim: Al-Tameemi and Rodríguez-Verdugo 2024 report two P putida morphotypes persisting about 150 generations only in A johnsonii co-culture.
caveat: The original 200-generation experiment is a reused earlier dataset and persistence of two lineages is not a co-reproducing group.

claim: Reciprocal invasion did not support hypothesized frequency-dependent maintenance; a matched externally supplemented benzoate evolution control was absent.
caveat: Observed diversity could partly reflect resource flux/population size rather than partner-specific new ecological opportunity.

claim: Pauli et al. 2022 authors report obligately cross-feeding E coli generally less able to adapt to stepwise antibiotics than nutrient-supplemented monocultures.
caveat: E1 source-level methods excerpts only; chemical dependencies and stresses specific to this bacterial system.

claim: Melero-Jiménez et al. 2025 report >80% recovery among abruptly stressed obligate mutualist populations but only one partner persisted after bypassing nutritional auxotrophy.
caveat: Survivor recovery means failure of collective partnership, not emergent higher organism; full per-stress numerator E2 audit outstanding.

claim: Athreya et al. 2025 theoretical study separates mutual dependence from reproductive cohesion, with dependence sometimes arising faster than synchronized reproduction.
caveat: Publisher abstract only, mathematical not biological experiment; the main article is not fully accessible/reviewed here.

claim: Black et al. 2020 show ecological patch, regeneration and dispersal structure can mathematically confer collective-level selection properties.
caveat: Externally imposed patch structure is evolutionary scaffolding, not the spontaneous creation of heritable collective boundaries.

claim: A johnsonii leaks benzoate from benzyl-alcohol metabolism and P putida can consume it, providing a concrete ecological cross-feeding mechanism.
caveat: Unidirectional commensal cross-feeding is not experimentally proven obligate mutualism or evolved group co-transmission.

claim: Protein translation inhibitors reportedly accelerate Stentor habituation and delay responsiveness recovery.
caveat: Drug-specific motor changes, excluded detached cells and mechanism specificity remain unresolved.

claim: Stentor habituated response reportedly persists into at least some daughter cells after cell division.
caveat: Carrier and number of generations unclear; not DNA sequence change or conscious experience.

claim: SteCoe_6763 RNAi, calcium and broad kinase inhibitors affect Stentor habituation dynamics.
caveat: KN-93 also targets ion channels and unrelated pathways; cannot isolate CaMKII from inhibitor response.

claim: Single Stentor cells can switch rapidly between responsive states while a population mean changes gradually.
caveat: Two-state fit describes behavior but does not show a unique molecular circuit.

claim: Receptor-inactivation model predicts weak/strong Stentor challenge and response recovery patterns, partly confirmed.
caveat: Receptor-number memory is a model hypothesis, not definitive biochemical proof.

claim: BioRxiv 2026 reports Stentor habituation frequency slope near negative thirty dB per decade.
caveat: Early preprint, not replicated or peer reviewed, and stimulus protocol may differ.

claim: Physarum habituates to quinine and caffeine and returns to avoidance after stimulus removal.
caveat: Only simple non-neural habituation; no demonstration of general intelligence or transmitted offspring.

claim: Physarum salt-trained controls showed habituation over five days and recovery after two salt-free days.
caveat: This behavior alone cannot identify a specific memory molecule.

claim: Physarum behavior transferred into formerly naive recipient after three-hour fusion and separation but not after one hour.
caveat: Horizontal fusion and cell transfer are not offspring, and physical transport mediator remains unknown.

claim: Physarum fusion composite group responses were nonlinear in the fraction of trained donors.
caveat: Nonlinear responses do not uniquely exclude physiological dilution or medium carryover.

claim: Physarum changes tube-diameter transport hierarchy in response to past nutrient stimuli.
caveat: Softening agent is a model inference; morphology changes may be passive rather than associative cognition.

claim: Microbial networks can exhibit anticipatory gene expression under selected temperature and oxygen correlations.
caveat: These results include evolution over generations, not novel within-life conditioning of fixed-genotype cells.

claim: In E coli and yeast, naturally selected early environmental cues can induce responses to later conditions.
caveat: Genetically programmed anticipation differs from new memory learned individually.

claim: Stentor drug-treatment detachment and contraction exclusions could bias the measured magnitude of habituation.
caveat: Published high-force/electrical controls do not remove all possible motor-response confounding.

claim: The original 2012 Physarum Y-maze study reports 39 of 40 plasmodia preferred an arm without extracellular slime over an arm with slime.
caveat: Slime avoidance is an existing biological response; does not establish a self-generated new memory encoding program or unique personal trail recognition.

claim: In the original U-shaped navigation test, 23/24 slime molds reached food on clean agar versus 8/24 on background slime-coated agar within 120 hours.
caveat: Extracellular background coating masked informative trail contrast; shared lab stock and imposed trap cannot be treated as independent evolved organisms.

claim: In the U-trap study, locomotion speed and food finding without the trap were not significantly altered by slime coating, strengthening a specific navigation-history mechanism.
caveat: Does not rule out every chemical/slime surface effect and does not prove internal modeling or task-general intelligence.

claim: Caudron and Barral 2013 report yeast Whi3 super-assemblies maintaining a mating-pheromone-refractory state after a deceptive courtship attempt.
caveat: Original complete paper methods not inspected here; later first-daughter findings show transmission is not absolutely excluded.

claim: 2022 Lau et al. report Whi3-associated bud fluorescence in about 24 percent of WT buds versus roughly 62 to 65 percent in three ER barrier-defective mutant groups.
caveat: Fluorescent aggregate localization is not fitness; mutations change multiple membrane and cellular functions.

claim: 2022 experimental gating studies show roughly half of first daughters but far fewer later daughters inherit altered mating response, while breaking barriers increases daughter memory inheritance.
caveat: Mother cell history and daughter order matter, and the effect was produced via experimental mutants not via observed spontaneous evolution of a memory gate.

claim: 2022 Whi3 tethering to a spindle-pole structure caused a larger fraction of yeast daughters to inherit altered pheromone responsiveness, up to 70.3 percent.
caveat: Engineered molecular inheritance does not show that copying more memory improves group-level survival or evolves autonomously.

claim: 2023 Akhtar et al. measured WT first/second daughter refractoriness 46.5 and 12.2 percent versus Shs1-defective 66.9 and 30.4 percent.
caveat: Shs1 disruption simultaneously alters mother escape, cell size and division timing, which can confound long-term fitness comparisons.

claim: 2023 septin imaging found aberrant localization in a substantial fraction of first post-escape divisions, coincident with larger attached daughters and weaker ER barrier.
caveat: Causal molecular trigger remains unknown; experimental group and basic organism overlap 2022 publication.

claim: A September 2026 revised Stentor bioRxiv preprint reports weak-strong timed stimulus pairing transiently increases contraction to weak taps beyond several nonpaired controls.
caveat: Not peer reviewed; same mechanosensory modality at two intensities, limited ecological transfer and no subjective awareness assay.

claim: 2008 Physarum work reports reduced movement near the expected next periodic adverse event after a short training sequence of periodic environmental stresses.
caveat: Simple phase-coupled oscillators could display similar behavior; irregular hidden-sequence and task-general fitness validation absent.

claim: Bruna and Gyllingberg 2025 describe an investigator-specified non-neural allostatic reservoir model that repeats periodic input patterns after stimulation ends.
caveat: Author-designed hexagonal grid and regulatory dynamics, not a natural organism or spontaneously discovered memory circuitry.

claim: Solé and Pla-Mauri 2025 derive transport conductance structure on fixed source-sink graphs from an energy-minimization-inspired Lagrangian.
caveat: Model uses externally imposed flow network and task constraints; no direct evidence of cognitive planning or memory inheritance.

claim: Adamatzky 2017 offers primary theoretical critique that many celebrated maze-solvers use physical least-resistance routes or chemoattractant gradients.
caveat: This is not direct empirical falsification of Reid 2012's trail-specific masking experiment and controls.

claim: Pla-Mauri and Solé 2026 report computer-designed regulatory motifs mimicking habituation, sensitization and massed-spaced training responses.
caveat: Engineered and simulated circuits are not spontaneously evolved mechanisms and were not demonstrated as an autonomously functioning wet-lab organism.

claim: The 2026 engineered-cognition paper cites openly available code and describes design components such as transcription factors and quorum sensing, but not organismal autonomy.
caveat: Even a reproduced circuit training curve would not prove adaptive generalization to unseen ecologies or subjective consciousness.

claim: A 2022 Whi3 forced daughter-transfer experiment increased inherited pheromone resistance, showing that memory segregation can be manipulated separately from the original maternal training stimulus.
caveat: Transport intervention may bring unrelated proteins or division effects; daughter behavior does not establish benefit under new ecological conditions.

claim: The 2023 follow-up observed that first daughter cells are bigger and more often remain attached to mothers, correlated with septin defects and memory propagation.
caveat: Repeated daughter observations are nested within mother histories and overlapping research group, not independent evolution cohorts.

claim: First glucose-to-lactose shift produces roughly 35-minute growth lag and 55-minute full recovery in chemoflux E coli.
caveat: Native metabolic machinery and researcher-supplied alternating media prevent claims of newly evolved learning.

claim: Lac protein carryover makes later exposure to lactose less costly, with memory fading through dilution over cell divisions.
caveat: Persistent physiology is not an organism inventing its own forgetting controller or mental representation.

claim: Response memory can boost lactose use by up to 100 percent under fast fluctuations according to the authors' mathematical model.
caveat: This is a modeled lactose flux difference, not a measured two-fold cell survival or lifetime fitness improvement.

claim: The authors find 53 percent of environmental component-history fitness measurements exceed their conservative significance threshold.
caveat: Percentage is of their defined pooled fitness assay observations, not independently created living organisms.

claim: The other static environment better predicts a current fluctuating-component fitness measurement in 29 percent of studied cases.
caveat: This is a statistical performance reversal under previous exposure, not conscious forecasting or an active learned goal.

claim: Only one or two original evolution flasks per condition contributed to the 889 selected barcoded mutants analyzed using three fitness assay replicates.
caveat: Do not treat the hundreds of barcodes or pooled fitness measurements as hundreds of independent evolutionary origins.

claim: Bacillus sporulation-reporter response carries roughly 1.96 bits of short-time history and 0.8813 bits at the final finite measurement window.
caveat: The maximum 3.3219 bits reflects ten investigator-selected past conditions, not a physical limit on memory or a life score.

claim: The authors explicitly consider metabolic initial state as an alternative to an evolved future-predictive strategy.
caveat: High mutual information about past conditions does not establish causal ecological benefit, intentional prediction or subjective experience.

claim: Receptor methylation and demethylation can implement integral feedback that restores adapted bacterial chemotaxis output after stimulation.
caveat: Existing sensor network and model assumptions are specified; it does not show the organism invented adaptive learning circuitry.

claim: Robust return of a chemotactic output to baseline is compatible with a hidden physical history state maintained within signaling machinery.
caveat: A smooth feedback response can look intelligent without novel learning, subjective experience or evolutionary self-creation.

claim: Engineered fast yeast phenotype switchers outgrow slow switchers when environments fluctuate frequently, and slow switchers win when changes are rare.
caveat: Constructed genetic circuits and experimenter-controlled cycles preexist; fitness differences do not prove cells learned the schedule.

claim: Model-predicted memory age/erasure policy and phenotypic switching costs have different benefits under periodic versus permanent environmental changes.
caveat: 2025 bioRxiv preprint NOT PEER REVIEWED; numerical strategy is authored, not a new biological learning experiment.

claim: Authors report minutes-to-hours history effects in individual E coli growth under repeated microfluidic nutrient changes.
caveat: Only publisher abstract and public selected descriptions reviewed; author term emergent learning is not a complete-method audit.

claim: The 2022 review describes history-dependent microbial lag and responses tied to previous nutrient, metabolite and phenotypic conditions.
caveat: Synthesis of prior results, not a separate biological experiment, and history dependence need not be task-general intelligence.

claim: Authors report 341 habituation-associated temporally regulated Stentor genes including candidate cyclic-nucleotide kinase processes.
caveat: July 2026 bioRxiv preprint NOT PEER REVIEWED; pooled transcriptomics do not prove unique molecular storage or consciousness.

claim: Gallie et al. 2015 reconstructed the molecular basis of a Pseudomonas colony switch derived from earlier experimental evolution and implicated existing metabolic bistability.
caveat: The original evolved switching population is also discussed in Beaumont 2009; reconstructing mechanism is not a fresh independent origin of the phenotype.

claim: The high capsule-producing state in the studied Pseudomonas system carried an approximately three-percent growth penalty in one tested condition.
caveat: The penalty is conditional on that genotype and assay; metabolic phenotype and fitness differences cannot be extrapolated to every artificial chemistry.

claim: The 2015 study found an analogous genetic modification in a standard E coli background failed to reproduce the same visually detectable colony-switching phenotype.
caveat: Genetic context matters, and this negative comparison prevents claiming a universally transferable switch module across species.

claim: Basan et al. 2020 reported pronounced growth-recovery delays after certain resource changes and a resource-allocation trade-off between fast current growth and future metabolic readiness.
caveat: The measured delays concern native metabolic pathways under researcher-supplied nutrient shifts and do not establish spontaneously evolved cognition.

claim: Manipulating metabolic enzyme readiness before a nutrient transition shortened subsequent E coli recovery lag under tested source-to-destination conditions.
caveat: The experiment altered enzyme expression deliberately; it demonstrates a causal biochemical readiness mechanism, not a naturally invented memory controller.

claim: The Basan study considered 144 specified nutrient transitions and reported some lags lasting up to approximately ten hours.
caveat: One hundred forty-four resource transitions are conditions within a study, not independent evolution populations or new organism origins.

claim: The 2026 Kratz full article describes single-cell E coli physiological adaptation under nutrient pulses, finding more frequent pulse histories associated with faster fitted growth adaptation.
caveat: The reported fitted time constant is extracted from averaged trajectories; approximately thirty thousand nested cells are not thirty thousand independent evolution experiments.

claim: Kratz et al. 2026 compare a Markovian resource-allocation model with a fractional-order history model using a researcher-defined memory response to past nutrient perturbations.
caveat: The mathematical memory kernel and sigmoid-gated estimator are model choices, not experimentally observed evolution of such algorithms inside bacteria.

claim: The proposed ribosomal-subsector distribution could explain multiple relaxation times in bacterial growth, but direct verification of those subpopulations is identified as a future experiment.
caveat: A plausible mechanistic model and RNN analogy do not constitute molecular proof, trained language cognition, or subjective experience.

claim: Beaumont and collaborators reported de novo stochastic phenotype switching in two of twelve independently evolved Pseudomonas populations under alternating selection.
caveat: Researcher-defined selection pressure and historical contingency produced a genetic population-level trait; it does not show a single cell learning future conditions.

claim: The 2009 switching lineage exhibited historical dependence of a late switch-related mutation on earlier inherited background changes.
caveat: The 2015 Gallie paper follows overlapping ancestral lineages and cannot be counted as a second independent evolution of the same event.

claim: Fridman and colleagues reported population evolution of delayed bacterial regrowth strategies tuned to historical stress intervals.
caveat: The finding concerns genotype-level biological selection across generations and is not evidence of personal learning, consciousness, or a general digital memory mechanism.

claim: Van den Bergh and collaborators reported that bacterial persistence evolved under recurrent stress schedules, but reversal after stress stopped was slower and incomplete.
caveat: Treatment-frequency response and loss of persistence are population-evolution phenomena, not adaptive erasure by an individual intelligent controller.

claim: The 2010 awakening study found the apparent fraction of dormant bacteria can change with the conditions used to measure resumption of growth.
caveat: Observer-defined assay timing and medium affect classification; results do not establish an intrinsic memory frequency independent of context.

claim: Reconstruction of the evolved switch supports a link between genotype accessibility and preexisting central metabolic branching behavior.
caveat: Molecular bistability depends on detailed biological scaffolding, and no new primitive reaction law or autonomous group reproduction was demonstrated.

claim: Two of twelve independently selected Pseudomonas bacterial lines evolved heritable stochastic colony switching under an externally imposed novelty-exclusion and single founder selection regime.
caveat: Only two entire independent source lines succeeded; the novelty exclusion and bottleneck were experimenter-installed, not endogenous evolution of a novel scoring system.

claim: Mutant carB was necessary for switching in one evolved genetic background, while in the original ancestor it also produced the phenotype but its fitness effect was unfavorable.
caveat: Physical expression of a phenotype was possible in the earlier background; its selectable survival benefit required earlier potentiation, so do not claim strict physical inaccessibility.

claim: Switching recurred in three of thirty-six one-round replays from a potentiated ancestor versus zero of 138 from the original ancestor, and persistence failed when the novelty exclusion reward was changed.
caveat: Replay assays are one-round tests, not 174 independent full evolutionary histories; removing the special selection changes the exact research ecology.

claim: Acar et al. engineered a yeast GAL regulatory switching network with experimentally chosen fast and slow rates rather than observing the switching policy spontaneously evolve.
caveat: Researchers explicitly designed switch rates and opposite fitness environments; this is an installed controller positive-control model, not endogenous intelligence.

claim: Fast switching showed an experimentally measured advantage during short switching schedules whereas slower switching was advantageous during longer environmental dwell times.
caveat: Fitness measurements are specific to two chosen schedules and genetically engineered growth reporter states, not a generally learned optimal policy.

claim: In one yeast environment transition, the faster switching configuration regained steady growth about four hours earlier but later paid a steady-state growth disadvantage.
caveat: The measured adaptation trade-off is population dynamics of preconfigured gene circuitry, not conscious anticipation by individual yeast cells.

claim: Hayden and colleagues' diversified RNA lines adapted about eightfold and sixfold faster than undiversified WT on an experimentally selected new substrate at the authors' generation-five rate comparison.
caveat: Two originally diversified ribozyme lines and descendant novel-substrate arms remain dependent on researcher-supplied transcription, mutagenesis and selection.

claim: An individually inactive AzoDelta ribozyme genotype recovered catalytic action when an alternative active ribozyme was supplied in the same assay.
caveat: Transient partner-enabled catalytic function does not establish a new collective life cycle or independently viable group offspring.

claim: Prior neutral mutations allowed RNA populations to approach genotype regions with higher activity after a substrate change even though those mutations lacked earlier native-function advantage.
caveat: A designed new-substrate assay and purifying selection create the tested fitness regime; no spontaneous niche selection or artificial general intelligence was demonstrated.

claim: Karve and Wagner compared bacterial backgrounds with roughly twenty-twofold mutation-rate difference and found more accumulated mutations without corresponding significant gain in newly viable phenotype count across five simple conditions.
caveat: These are externally screened viability environments, and original strains differed in baseline phenotypes; negative result does not imply mutation rate never matters.

claim: The published E coli assays associated greater environmental complexity with more latent new viability phenotypes, with reported rank correlations of approximately 0.87 and 0.82 in low and high mutation backgrounds.
caveat: Complex selection lasted roughly 600 versus 100–200 generations, and only one five-factor setting was examined; controls partially address duration rather than eliminating it.

claim: Pleiotropic regulatory and transport mutations were enriched in complex-environment selected samples and plausibly accounted for broad additional viability under novel assays.
caveat: Not every phenotypic gain was traced to a causal reconstructed allele, and all novelty types were investigator-defined pre-existing assay conditions.

claim: Rotrattanadumrong and Yokobayashi experimentally measured all 65,536 intermediate sequence combinations spanning 16 differences between two active ligase ribozyme variants.
caveat: The assay threshold defining neutral pathways was chosen by the researchers; 65,536 sequence variants are not independent living organisms.

claim: The ribozyme research combined over 120,000 experimentally screened RNA sequences with a final neural-model-guided computational selection stage involving 100 in-silico rounds.
caveat: External classifier labels and genetic-search algorithms directed discovery; it does not show RNA organisms training or autonomously evolving their own evaluation rules.

claim: Experimentally identified ribozyme neutral paths demonstrate that distant functional genotypes can remain connected through intermediate variants above a predefined assay activity cutoff.
caveat: Neutral connectivity within a sixteen-site bounded RNA assay does not guarantee similar viable ecological transitions or new reproduction mechanisms.

claim: Graham and colleagues report evolved Neurospora dormancy fractions rising with experimental bad-year frequency across 88 evolution samples derived from twelve genetic lineages.
caveat: The series prohibited consecutive adverse years and the 50 percent schedule was alternating, so natural unpredictability was intentionally constrained.

claim: The Neurospora study's final dormancy responses were better fit by a geometric-mean-fitness interpretation than by an arithmetic-mean alternative under the authors' chosen statistical comparison.
caveat: Relative support does not mean every line reached an evolutionary optimum, and multiple sampled lineages became extinct under small-founder transfer.

claim: Zheng and colleagues' published Science abstract reports cryptic sequence variation allowed selected fluorescent proteins to reach more diverse and better-performing genotype peaks.
caveat: E1 primary abstract only, externally chosen color/fluorescence trait and directed evolution, not a spontaneously self-sustaining collective program.

claim: Copley, Newton and Widney's review reports a median promiscuous enzyme side-reaction catalytic efficiency near 31 inverse-molar-seconds across 108 enzymes.
caveat: Cross-study enzyme review, not 108 new independent evolution populations; many such weak side activities cannot support meaningful fitness-related metabolic flux.

claim: The 2009 evolutionary-switch experiment found that when colonies produced by switching were no longer specially favored at transfer, the switching genotype was outcompeted.
caveat: This is a change in researcher-installed ecological selection, not proof that switching is impossible in all natural or theoretical environments.
